sources_considered.why: Official model card reports the factuality benchmark results and their metric definition.
Contemporaneous technical report corroborates the benchmark result, acknowledges hallucination limitations and supplies favorable peer comparisons.
Submission history establishes that version 2 was public on July 19, 2023.
Contemporaneous original experiment supplies favorable counterevidence, with a narrower factuality-recognition task.
Later evaluation does not directly measure the selected July–August 2023 period.

evidence_items.locator: Evaluation Results, fine-tuned models safety table
evidence_items.explanation: The 70B chat model achieved 64.14% generations judged both truthful and informative on TruthfulQA, showing a substantial gap from reliable factual answering. This result is also present in the dated July technical report; unsuccessful answers cannot all be counted as hallucinations.

evidence_items.locator: Section 4.2, Truthfulness, Toxicity, and Bias; section 5.2, Limitations and Ethical Considerations
evidence_items.explanation: The report ranks Llama 2-Chat favorably against these peers while separately acknowledging a propensity to hallucinate in section 5.2. It supports the reliability concern but weighs against reading Marcus as claiming inferior performance relative to competitors.

Anyscale found strong performance by Llama-2-70b when choosing between correct and incorrect summaries. Recognizing a supplied factual summary differs from generating one without hallucinations, so this is material context rather than direct contradiction.

unresolved_gaps: These sources do not establish a representative real-world hallucination rate across all Meta LLM uses.
